人教版选择性必修 1 · 第三章第二节「气压带和风带」（p.48–53），第三节: PEP Elective Vol. 1 · Ch. 3, Sec. 2 “Pressure Belts and Wind Belts” (pp. 48–53), Sec. 3 case study (pp. 56–57)
气压带、风带与三圈环流: Pressure Belts, Wind Belts and the Three-Cell Circulation
麦哲伦船队为什么有的航段逆风、有的顺风，到了 30°S 附近却寸步难行？: Why did Magellan's fleet face headwinds on some legs and tailwinds on others, yet barely move near 30°S?
赤道受热上升 → 赤道低压带: Equator heated, air rises → equatorial low-pressure belt
30° 堆积下沉 · 60° 暖空气爬升 → 三圈: Sinking pile-up at 30° · warm air rising at 60° → three cells
七个气压带 · 六个风带 · 绕地一圈: Seven pressure belts · six wind belts · all the way around the globe
随直射点夏北冬南 → 交替控制: Follow the direct-sun point north in summer, south in winter → alternating control
陆地冬冷夏热 → 气压中心 → 季风: Land colder in winter, hotter in summer → pressure centers → monsoons
0°–30°：赤道上升 · 30° 下沉: 0°–30°: rises at the equator · sinks at 30°
60°–90°：60° 爬升 · 极地下沉: 60°–90°: rises at 60° · sinks at the pole
赤道为什么是一条低压带？: Why is the equator a low-pressure belt?
拖动视角绕地球看一圈：剖面里，赤道上空的琥珀色箭头往上升: Drag to rotate the view around the globe: in the cross-section, the amber arrows above the equator rise upward
赤道近地面的空气受热上升，剖面里低纬环流的上升支（琥珀色）从赤道升起: Air near the surface at the equator is heated and rises; in the cross-section, the rising branch of the low-latitude cell (amber) climbs from the equator
受热不均 + 地转偏向力 → 大气环流: Uneven heating + Coriolis force → atmospheric circulation
教材假设：地球表面是均匀的: Textbook assumption: Earth's surface is uniform
赤道地区接受太阳辐射能量多，近地面空气受热膨胀上升，空气密度减小，气压降低。: The equatorial region receives a lot of solar energy; air near the surface is heated, expands and rises, its density falls, and the pressure drops.
教材假设地球表面是均匀的：引起大气运动的只有高、低纬度的受热不均和地转偏向力。: The textbook assumes Earth's surface is uniform: the only things driving air movement are uneven heating between high and low latitudes and the Coriolis force.
赤道低压带是热力成因：由冷热差异直接造成。: The equatorial low-pressure belt is thermal in origin: it is caused directly by temperature differences.
去掉这一步：不知道大气为什么会动起来，后面的三个环流圈都无从谈起。: Without this step: you don't know why the air moves at all, and the three circulation cells that follow have no basis.
常考：赤道低压带、极地高压带是热力成因；副热带高压带、副极地低压带是动力成因。: Frequently tested: the equatorial low and polar high are thermal in origin; the subtropical high and subpolar low are dynamic in origin.
赤道接受的太阳辐射多，近地面空气受热膨胀上升、气压降低，形成赤道低压带（热力成因: The equator receives a lot of solar radiation; air near the surface is heated, expands and rises, and the pressure drops, forming the equatorial low-pressure belt (thermal origin).
升上去的空气，为什么走到 30° 就下沉？: Why does the air that rose sink once it reaches 30°?
点一下剖面（或环流圈），从赤道上空放出一团空气，看它在高空一边向北走、一边向右偏: Click the cross-section (or a circulation cell) to release a parcel of air above the equator, and watch it drift to the right as it moves north aloft
气团先偏成西南风，到 30°N 高空偏成西风，在那里堆积下沉；虚线是「如果不偏转: The parcel first turns into a southwest wind, becomes a westerly aloft at 30°N, and piles up and sinks there; the dashed line is the path it would take “without deflection” — all the way to the pole
地转偏向力：北半球右偏 · 南半球左偏 · 赤道不偏: Coriolis force: right in the Northern Hemisphere · left in the Southern · none at the equator
30°N 高空：气流偏成西风 → 堆积下沉: Aloft at 30°N: flow turns westerly → piles up and sinks
赤道上升的暖空气在高空向南北分流；向北的一支逐渐右偏成西南风，到北纬 30° 附: Warm air rising at the equator splits north and south aloft; the northward branch gradually turns right into a southwest wind, and near 30°N aloft it becomes a westerly.
空气在这里不断堆积下沉，使地面气压升高，形成副热带高压带（动力成因）。: Air keeps piling up and sinking here, raising surface pressure and forming the subtropical high-pressure belt (dynamic origin).
下沉后近地面分两支：向南右偏成东北信风，向北右偏成西南风（盛行西风）；东北信风与: After sinking, the surface flow splits in two: southward it turns right into the northeast trades, northward it turns right into a southwest wind (the prevailing westerlies); the northeast and southeast trades converge and rise at the equator.
去掉偏转：气流会一路流到极地（虚线），不会在 30° 附近堆积下沉，也就没有副热: Remove the deflection: the flow would run all the way to the pole (dashed line), wouldn't pile up and sink near 30°, and there would be no subtropical high-pressure belt.
易错：副热带高压带不是冷却下沉形成的，是高空气流堆积下沉（动力成因）。: Common mistake: the subtropical high-pressure belt isn't formed by air cooling and sinking; it forms when air aloft piles up and sinks (dynamic origin).
地转偏向力让高空气流在 30° 附近偏成西风，空气堆积下沉，形成副热带高压带；东: The Coriolis force turns the flow aloft into a westerly near 30°, where air piles up and sinks, forming the subtropical high-pressure belt; the northeast and southeast trades converge and rise at the equator, completing the low-latitude cell.
60° 附近为什么又出现一条低压带？: Why is there another low-pressure belt near 60°?
点剖面里 60°N 的「极锋」: Click the “polar front” at 60°N in the cross-section
暖而轻的盛行西风沿极锋爬升到冷而重的极地东风之上；中纬、高纬两个环流圈闭合，中纬: The warm, light prevailing westerlies climb along the polar front over the cold, dense polar easterlies; the mid- and high-latitude cells close up, and the mid-latitude cell turns opposite to the other two
暖而轻的盛行西风 → 爬升到冷而重的极地东风之上: Warm, light prevailing westerlies → climb over the cold, dense polar easterlies
北极终年寒冷，空气堆积下沉，形成极地高压带；向南流的气流右偏成东北风，叫极地东风: The Arctic is cold all year, so air piles up and sinks there, forming the polar high-pressure belt; flow heading south turns right into a northeast wind, called the polar easterlies.
极地东风在北纬 60° 附近与较暖的盛行西风相遇，暖空气爬升，在两条高压带之间形: Near 60°N the polar easterlies meet the warmer prevailing westerlies; the warm air climbs, forming a relatively low-pressure belt between the two high-pressure belts — the subpolar low-pressure belt (dynamic origin).
低纬环流、高纬环流由冷热差异直接驱动；中纬环流夹在中间被带动，方向与两侧相反。: The low- and high-latitude cells are driven directly by temperature differences; the mid-latitude cell, sandwiched between them, is dragged along and turns the opposite way.
去掉这一步：中纬、高纬两个环流圈都不成立，北半球只剩一个低纬环流圈。: Without this step: neither the mid- nor the high-latitude cell holds up, leaving the Northern Hemisphere with only a low-latitude cell.
易错：副极地低压带不是受热上升形成的，是冷暖气流相遇、暖空气爬升（动力成因）。: Common mistake: the subpolar low-pressure belt isn't formed by heated air rising; it forms where cold and warm flows meet and the warm air climbs (dynamic origin).
暖空气沿极锋爬升，形成副极地低压带（动力成因）；北半球由此有三个环流圈，南半球同: Warm air climbs along the polar front, forming the subpolar low-pressure belt (dynamic origin); this gives the Northern Hemisphere three circulation cells, and the Southern Hemisphere has three as well.

七个气压带、六个风带，是一条线还是绕地球一圈？: Are the seven pressure belts and six wind belts lines, or rings around the globe?

C + H₂O(g) → CO + H₂，吸热，把煤变成组成可调的气: C + H₂O(g) → CO + H₂, endothermic: turns coal into a gas of adjustable composition

Copper wire and graphite are elements; ionization needs no current (Required Vol. 1 p. 20 Exercise 2).
H₂SO₄ 要写 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻；弱电解质 CH₃COOH 用可逆号；K: H₂SO₄ must be written as 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻; the weak electrolyte CH₃COOH uses a reversible arrow; the nitrate ion in KNO₃ is NO₃⁻. Strong electrolytes ionize completely and use an equals sign (Required Vol. 1 p. 16).
同体积、同浓度的盐酸与醋酸，导电能力差别明显，主要原因是: Hydrochloric acid and acetic acid of the same volume and concentration differ clearly in conductivity, mainly because
醋酸不与水混合: acetic acid doesn't mix with water
醋酸只有部分电离，溶液中离子浓度小: acetic acid only partly ionizes, so its ion concentration is low
醋酸分子比盐酸分子大: acetic acid molecules are bigger than hydrochloric acid molecules
盐酸是酸，醋酸不是酸: hydrochloric acid is an acid, acetic acid isn't
导电能力取决于自由移动离子的浓度与电荷。HCl 全部电离，CH₃COOH 只有约: Conductivity depends on the concentration and charge of freely moving ions. HCl ionizes completely, while only about 1.32% of CH₃COOH ionizes (α = √(Ka/c)), so its ion concentration is much lower (Elective Vol. 1 Experiment 3-1).
向 Ba(OH)₂ 溶液中逐滴加入稀硫酸，导电能力先减小后增大的原因是: When dilute sulfuric acid is added drop by drop to Ba(OH)₂ solution, conductivity first decreases and then increases because
BaSO₄ 不是电解质，生成的沉淀不导电: BaSO₄ is not an electrolyte, so the precipitate doesn't conduct
Ba²⁺ 与 OH⁻ 被沉淀和中和带走，恰好完全反应时离子最少，之后过量的稀硫酸: Ba²⁺ and OH⁻ are removed by precipitation and neutralization, ions are fewest at exact complete reaction, and after that the excess dilute sulfuric acid ionizes to supply ions
水的量增加了，所以导电能力变大: the amount of water increased, so conductivity rose
温度升高使离子运动加快: the temperature rose, making the ions move faster
BaSO₄ 难溶但溶解的部分完全电离，它仍是强电解质；导电能力下降是因为溶液中自: BaSO₄ is insoluble, but the part that dissolves ionizes completely, so it is still a strong electrolyte; conductivity drops because the freely moving ions in solution are removed by precipitation and neutralization. 铁钉生锈消耗了试管内的氧气，管内压强变小: Rusting of the nail uses up oxygen in the tube, lowering the pressure
试管里的空气受热膨胀: The air in the tube expands when heated
铁钉与水反应放出气体: The nail reacts with water to release a gas

生铁更硬，表面更容易开裂: Pig iron is harder, so its surface cracks more easily
纯铁表面有一层保护膜: Pure iron has a protective film on its surface
生铁里的碳会直接与氧气反应: The carbon in pig iron reacts directly with oxygen
不纯的金属才与电解质溶液构成原电池：钢铁里的铁和少量单质碳构成原电池，铁作负极被: Only impure metals form galvanic cells with an electrolyte: in steel, iron and a little elemental carbon form a cell, with iron as the anode being oxidized and carbon as the cathode (Elective Vol. 1, pp. 111–112). Step 3 of this lesson shows this as “58 mm with carbon vs 23 mm without”.
关于暖贴的发热原理与使用，正确的是: Which statement about how a hand warmer heats and how to use it is correct?
暖贴靠活性炭吸附放热: A hand warmer releases heat through adsorption on activated carbon
暖贴靠铁的吸氧腐蚀放热，捂着用会更热: A hand warmer releases heat through oxygen-absorption corrosion of iron, and gets hotter if covered
暖贴靠铁的吸氧腐蚀放热，必须有氧气，不能捂实: A hand warmer releases heat through oxygen-absorption corrosion of iron, needs oxygen, and must not be covered tightly
暖贴里的食盐水是燃料: The salt water in a hand warmer is the fuel
教材研究与实践：暖贴「利用金属的电化学腐蚀原理制作」——铁粉被氧化的放热过程；正: Textbook Research and Practice: hand warmers are “made using the principle of electrochemical corrosion of metals” — heat released as iron powder is oxidized; the cathode needs 2H₂O + O₂ + 4e⁻ = 4OH⁻, so no oxygen means no heat (Step 7 of this lesson: covered, 48.5 → 20.0 ℃).
锅炉内壁焊上锌片、或船体镶嵌锌块，依据的原理是: Zinc sheets welded to the inside of a boiler, or zinc blocks fitted to a ship's hull, work because
锌比铁活泼，作原电池负极被腐蚀，铁作正极被保护: Zinc is more active than iron, so it is the anode and corrodes while iron is the cathode and is protected
锌把铁表面完全隔绝了空气: Zinc completely seals the iron surface from air
锌与铁形成合金更耐腐蚀: Zinc and iron form a more corrosion-resistant alloy
牺牲阳极法：镁、锌比铁活泼，它们成为原电池的负极不断遭受腐蚀，作为正极的钢铁设备: Sacrificial anode method: magnesium and zinc are more active than iron, so they become the anode and keep corroding, while the steel equipment, as the cathode, is protected (Elective Vol. 1, p. 114). In Step 8 of this lesson the column still rises to 63 mm, but Fe²⁺ is not detected.
溶液换成饱和食盐水：中性水膜，走吸氧腐蚀，水柱上升: Solution changed to saturated salt water: neutral water film, oxygen-absorption corrosion, column rises
溶液换成稀盐酸：酸性水膜，改走析氢腐蚀，水柱被 H₂ 顶下: Solution changed to dilute HCl: acidic water film, switches to hydrogen-evolution corrosion, column pushed down by H₂
溶液换成蒸馏水：几乎没有离子，腐蚀慢得多: Solution changed to distilled water: almost no ions, corrosion much slower
已加入碳粉：碳作正极，O₂ 有地方得电子，腐蚀变快: Carbon added: carbon is the cathode, O₂ has somewhere to gain electrons, corrosion speeds up
未加碳粉：只有铁钉，几乎没有微电池，腐蚀很慢: No carbon: just the nail, almost no micro-cells, corrosion very slow
接触空气：吸氧腐蚀开始、暖贴开始发热: Open to air: oxygen-absorption corrosion starts, hand warmer starts heating
隔绝空气：没有 O₂，正极反应停、暖贴不发热: Sealed off: no O₂, cathode reaction stops, hand warmer doesn't heat
锌块接上：锌作负极被腐蚀，铁作正极被保护（Fe²⁺ 检验转阴性）: Zinc connected: zinc is the anode and corrodes, iron is the cathode and is protected (Fe²⁺ test turns negative)
锌块断开：铁的腐蚀恢复，Fe²⁺ 又能检出: Zinc disconnected: iron corrosion resumes, Fe²⁺ detected again

电流的磁场: Magnetic Field of an Electric Current
必修第三册 · 第十三章第 1 节「磁场 磁感线」（印刷页 p.104–108）: Required Vol. 3 · Ch. 13, Sec. 1 “Magnetic Fields and Field Lines” (printed p.104–108)
B̂ = Î × r̂ · 环与螺线管 B̂ = n̂: B̂ = Î × r̂ · loop and solenoid B̂ = n̂
磁场看不见摸不着，怎么把它画出来、又怎么判断它的方向？: A magnetic field can't be seen or touched. How do we draw it, and how do we tell its direction?
通电导线周围有磁场: A current-carrying wire has a magnetic field around it
铁屑排列 → 画出曲线，切线 = 方向: Iron filing pattern → draw curves; tangent = direction
一圈圈同心圆；右手握导线: Concentric circles; grip the wire with your right hand
穿环绕回的闭合曲线；右手握线圈: Closed curves that pass through and loop back; grip the coil with your right hand
疏密表示强弱：∝ I、N、1/r: Line density shows strength: ∝ I, N, 1/r
竖直导线周围是一圈圈同心圆: Concentric circles around a vertical wire
穿环绕回的闭合曲线，中间最强: Closed curves passing through and looping back, strongest in the middle
内部近似匀强，外部像条形磁体: Nearly uniform inside, like a bar magnet outside
看不见摸不着，凭什么说通电导线周围有磁场？: You can't see or touch it, so how can we say there's a magnetic field around a current-carrying wire?
打开三块玻璃板上的铁屑: Turn on the iron filings on the three glass plates
三块玻璃板上同时出现一层铁屑，沿磁场方向排成链：直导线周围排成一圈圈的圆；读数: A layer of iron filings appears on all three glass plates at once, lining up in chains along the field: around the straight wire they form circles; reading 20.0 μT (I = 2.0 A, r = 2.0 cm)
教材 A2.1 + A2.2 + A2.3：通电导线周围存在磁场（奥斯特 182: Textbook A2.1 + A2.2 + A2.3: a current-carrying wire has a magnetic field around it (Oersted, 1820); the field is invisible but real. Iron filings become tiny compass needles in the field, and after a light tap on the glass they line up in chains along the field lines, so they can reveal the field.
奥斯特 1820：通电导线使小磁针偏转，第一次揭示电与磁的联系（教材 p.104: Oersted, 1820: a current-carrying wire deflected a compass needle, the first link found between electricity and magnetism (textbook p.104–105).
磁场客观存在、不用接触就起作用；铁屑在磁场里被磁化成小磁针，轻敲玻璃板后沿磁感线: The magnetic field is real and acts without contact; iron filings become tiny compass needles in the field and, after a light tap on the glass, line up in chains along the field lines (the demo method on p.106).
铁屑分布只是示意：真实演示要用很大的电流（或多匝线圈）才排得出来，本课读数一律按: The filing pattern is schematic only: a real demo needs a very large current (or a multi-turn coil) to form it, while all readings here use 2 A. The textbook first uses a bar magnet for comparison and then switches to a straight wire; this lesson goes straight to three current-carrying setups.
去掉这一步：磁场变成「看不见也说不清存在」的空话，后面所有磁感线都没有依据。: Without this step, the magnetic field becomes empty talk about “something invisible we can't prove exists”, and none of the later field lines have any basis.
常考：奥斯特实验说明电流周围存在磁场（电流的磁效应）。: Common exam point: Oersted's experiment shows a current has a magnetic field around it (the magnetic effect of current).
直导线周围的磁感线是什么形状？: What shape are the field lines around a straight wire?
拖动视角绕导线转一圈，看整族同心圆: Drag to rotate the view around the wire and see the whole family of concentric circles
磁感线是一圈圈的同心圆，全部落在与导线垂直的水平面上；绕导线转到任何一侧都还是同: The field lines are concentric circles, all in horizontal planes perpendicular to the wire; from any side of the wire they are the same circles; reading 20.0 μT
教材 A2.7 原句：直线电流的磁感线是一圈圈的同心圆，这些同心圆都在跟导线垂直: Textbook A2.7: the field lines of a straight current are concentric circles, all in planes perpendicular to the wire. Field lines join end to end (closed); a page diagram shows just one plane of this family of circles.
B̂ ⊥ r̂，B̂ 沿绕轴圆周: B̂ ⊥ r̂, B̂ along the circle around the axis
纸面只是截面: The page is only a cross-section
同心圆，并且都在与导线垂直的平面上（教材 p.106 原句）。: Concentric circles, all in planes perpendicular to the wire (textbook p.106).
不是从导线沿半径射出去——那是点电荷的电场（A7.2 的错法）。: They don't radiate out from the wire along radii; that's the electric field of a point charge (the mistake in A7.2).
纸面图只是三维这一族圆的一个截面，绕轴转一圈才看全。: A page diagram is just one cross-section of this 3D family of circles; you need to go all the way around the axis to see it all.
去掉这一步：学生会照点电荷的样子把磁感线画成放射状。: Without this step, students draw field lines radiating outward like a point charge.
常考陷阱：直导线周围的磁感线沿半径向外（A7.2）。: Common exam trap: field lines around a straight wire point outward along radii (A7.2).
电流方向一反过来，磁感线的方向怎么变？: When the current reverses, how does the field direction change?
把电流拖到 −2.0 A（反向），盯住箭头和方向读数: Drag the current to −2.0 A (reversed) and watch the arrows and the direction reading
读数仍是 20.0 μT（大小不变），方向读数由「俯视逆时针」变成「俯视顺时针」: The reading stays 20.0 μT (same magnitude); the direction reading changes from “counterclockwise from above” to “clockwise from above”, every arrow on the circles flips, and the B arrow at the probe turns around
教材 A2.7 原句：用右手握住导线，让伸直的拇指所指的方向与电流方向一致，弯曲: Textbook A2.7: grip the wire with your right hand with your thumb along the current; your curled fingers show the direction the field lines circle. Reverse the current and the field direction at every point reverses. As a dot product: B̂·(Î×r̂) goes from +1 to −1.
右手握导线 · 图 13.1-7: Right hand grips the wire · Fig. 13.1-7
右手握导线：拇指沿电流、四指沿磁感线环绕方向。: Right hand grips the wire: thumb along the current, fingers along the direction the field lines circle.
电流反向 → 每一圈的绕向都反，而读数 20.0 μT 一点不变。: Reverse the current → every circle reverses direction, while the 20.0 μT reading doesn't change at all.
判据是 B̂·(Î×r̂)：反向前 +1、反向后 −1，不是「箭头掉头」那么简单: The criterion is B̂·(Î×r̂): +1 before reversing, −1 after; it's not as simple as “the arrow turns around”.
去掉这一步：学生以为反向只改磁场指向、不改环绕方向（A7.4 的错法）。: Without this step, students think reversing only changes where the field points, not the direction it circles (the mistake in A7.4).
常考：安培定则用右手；「握导线」与「握线圈」两套手势的手指角色互换（A7.3、A: Common exam point: Ampère's rule uses the right hand; in “grip the wire” and “grip the coil” the roles of thumb and fingers swap (A7.3, A7.12).
离导线越远，磁场为什么越弱？: Why is the field weaker farther from the wire?
把探点拖到 4.0 cm，比较两处的疏密与读数: Drag the probe to 4.0 cm and compare line density and readings at the two points
读数 20.0 → 10.0 μT（相对参考 1.00 → 0.50），相对地磁: Reading 20.0 → 10.0 μT (relative to reference 1.00 → 0.50), relative to Earth's field 0.40 → 0.20; the circles around the probe are clearly sparser
教材 A2.4：磁感线密的地方磁场强、疏的地方弱；直导线的 B 与到导线的距离成: Textbook A2.4: where field lines are dense the field is strong, where sparse it is weak; for a straight wire B is inversely proportional to distance (extension), so doubling r halves B. The same reading can be compared with the field strength table on textbook p.110: 20 μT is only 0.40 times Earth's average field of 50 μT.
拓展 · 按毕奥–萨伐尔定律计算: Extension · calculated with the Biot–Savart law
疏密表示强弱：密处强、疏处弱（教材 p.106 原句）。: Density shows strength: strong where dense, weak where sparse (textbook p.106).
r 从 2.0 到 4.0 cm，B 从 20.0 到 10.0 μT——变 1: r from 2.0 to 4.0 cm, B from 20.0 to 10.0 μT: it becomes 1/2, not 1/4.
20 μT 只有地磁场平均值 50 μT（教材 p.110）的 0.40 倍，真: 20 μT is only 0.40 times Earth's average field of 50 μT (textbook p.110); a real compass needle would be dominated by Earth's field, so this lesson uses iron filings.
去掉这一步：「疏密表示强弱」变成一句背下来的话。: Without this step, “density shows strength” is just a memorized sentence.
常考：距离变 2 倍，直导线的 B 变 1/2。: Common exam point: doubling the distance makes a straight wire's B 1/2.
环形电流的磁感线从哪里穿进去、又从哪里绕回来？: Where do a current loop's field lines pass through, and where do they loop back?
拖动视角绕环转一圈，看磁感线怎么穿进去再绕回: Drag to rotate the view around the loop and see how field lines pass through and loop back
过环轴的每个平面里都是一族闭合曲线：环内穿过环面、环外绕回，没有一个断口；中心读: In every plane through the loop's axis there is a family of closed curves: through the loop inside, looping back outside, with no break; center reading 25.1 μT, direction reading “toward the +x end”
教材 A2.8 + 图 13.1-9：环形电流的磁感线是一族闭合曲线，从环的一侧: Textbook A2.8 + Fig. 13.1-9: a current loop's field lines are a family of closed curves, coming out one side of the loop and looping back to the other. Use the other form of Ampère's rule: curl your right-hand fingers along the current, and your extended thumb points along the field on the axis (here, the +x end).
右手握线圈 · 图 13.1-10: Right hand grips the coil · Fig. 13.1-10
每条曲线都闭合：环内穿出、环外绕回。: Every curve is closed: out through the loop, back around the outside.
整族曲线绕环轴转一圈才是全部，纸面只有一个子午面。: The full family only appears when you go all the way around the loop's axis; the page shows just one meridian plane.
右手握线圈：四指沿电流、拇指沿轴线——和握导线时手指角色正好互换。: Right hand grips the coil: fingers along the current, thumb along the axis, the reverse roles from gripping a wire.
去掉这一步：学生会把环的磁感线画成上下两条直线，或者忘了它要绕回来。: Without this step, students draw a loop's field lines as two straight lines above and below, or forget that they loop back.
常考：环形电流中心的磁场方向由安培定则（握线圈）判定（A7.6）。: Common exam point: the field direction at a current loop's center is found with Ampère's rule (grip the coil) (A7.6).
把一匝变成十匝，中间的磁场变几倍？: Going from one turn to ten, by what factor does the field in the middle change?
中心读数 25.1 → 251 μT（相对参考 1.00 → 10.00）；磁感: Center reading 25.1 → 251 μT (relative to reference 1.00 → 10.00); the field-line shape doesn't change at all, it just gets denser and brighter
教材 A4.5 原句「通电螺线管可以看作许多匝环形电流串联而成」：每一匝对中心的: Textbook A4.5: “a current-carrying solenoid can be seen as many current loops in series”. Each turn adds to the center field in the same direction, so B is proportional to the number of turns (B₀ = μ0NI/(2R), extension), while the field-line shape stays the same.
多匝 = 串联的许多单匝，每一匝的贡献同向。: Many turns = many single turns in series, each adding in the same direction.
形状不变，只有疏密变——强弱变了、几何没变。: Same shape; only density changes. Strength changed, geometry didn't.
去掉这一步：学生把「匝数」和「形状」搅在一起，以为多绕几圈磁感线会变形。: Without this step, students mix up “number of turns” and “shape”, thinking more turns distort the field lines.
常考：匝数加倍、电流不变，中心 B 加倍。: Common exam point: double the turns with the same current, and B at the center doubles.
沿轴线往外走，磁场怎样变弱？: Moving outward along the axis, how does the field weaken?
把探点沿轴拖到 z = 5.0 cm（正好是环半径）: Drag the probe along the axis to z = 5.0 cm (exactly the loop radius)
读数 25.1 → 8.89 μT（相对参考 0.35）：z = R 处只剩中心: Reading 25.1 → 8.89 μT (0.35 relative to reference): at z = R only 0.354 of the center value remains; the direction reading is still “toward the +x end”, and the arrow just gets shorter
轴线上处处 B̂ = n̂（同一方向，只是变弱）：B(z) = B₀/(1+(z: On the axis B̂ = n̂ everywhere (same direction, just weaker): B(z) = B₀/(1+(z/R)²)^{3/2}. At z = R the factor is 0.354 (25.13 → 8.89 μT); at z = 2R only 0.089 remains.
轴线上处处沿轴：方向不变、只是变弱。: Along the axis everywhere: direction unchanged, just weaker.
去掉这一步：学生以为「离开环就没有磁场了」。: Without this step, students think “once you leave the loop there's no field”.
常考：由电流方向判轴线上各点的磁场方向（A7.14②）。: Common exam point: find the field direction at points on the axis from the current direction (A7.14②).
螺线管内部为什么近似匀强？管口外又弱到多少？: Why is the field inside a solenoid nearly uniform? And how weak is it beyond the end?
把探点拖到管口 z = 6.0 cm，再拖到 10.0 cm 看管外: Drag the probe to the solenoid end at z = 6.0 cm, then to 10.0 cm to see outside
中心 8128 μT、管口 z = 6.0 cm 处约 4160 μT（理论 4: Center 8128 μT, about 4160 μT at the end z = 6.0 cm (theory 4156, about half), only 248 μT outside at 10.0 cm; inside, field lines are nearly parallel and evenly spaced, thinning quickly near the end; N pole at the +x end
教材 A2.8 + A2.15 + 练习第 6 题：通电螺线管外部的磁场与条形磁: Textbook A2.8 + A2.15 + exercise 6: a solenoid's field outside is very like a bar magnet's, and nearly uniform inside (field lines are evenly spaced parallel lines); inside, field lines point from S to N, so the thumb direction (+x end) is the N pole. At the end only half the turns contribute, so it's about half the inside value (0.51).
内部近似匀强：磁感线平行、间隔相等（教材第 2 节的匀强磁场判据）。: Nearly uniform inside: field lines parallel and evenly spaced (the textbook Sec. 2 criterion for a uniform field).
中心 8128 μT、管口 4156 μT（0.51 倍）、管外 10.0 cm: Center 8128 μT, end 4156 μT (0.51×), only 248 μT outside at 10.0 cm.
内部磁感线由 S 极指向 N 极，拇指方向（+x 端）就是 N 极——外部与条形: Inside, field lines point from S to N, so the thumb direction (+x end) is the N pole; outside it's very like a bar magnet.
去掉这一步：「内部匀强」与「外部像条形磁体」变成两句互不相干的话。: Without this step, “uniform inside” and “like a bar magnet outside” become two unrelated sentences.
必考（教材练习第 6 题）：内部比管口外强，依据是磁感线疏密。: Must-know (textbook exercise 6): the field is stronger inside than just outside the end, judged by field-line density.
考核：在螺线管上找到读数正好是内部一半的位置: Test: find the point on the solenoid where the reading is exactly half the inside value
把探点从中心往外拖，让读数落在约 4160 μT（内部 8128 的一半），保持: Drag the probe outward from the center until the reading is about 4160 μT (half of the inside 8128), and hold for 10 s
读数降到约 4160 μT（理论 4156）时 z = 6.0 cm，正好落在管: When the reading drops to about 4160 μT (theory 4156), z = 6.0 cm, exactly at the end; the direction reading is still “toward the N pole (+x end)”
考核没有新结论：半值位置就是管口——「内部匀强、管口一半、外部像条形磁体」三件事: The test brings no new conclusion: the half-value point is the end. “Uniform inside, half at the end, like a bar magnet outside” come together in one device; strength is always judged by field-line density (textbook exercise 6).

海面上的水，为什么会自己走成一条条「河」？: Why does water on the sea surface flow on its own like a set of “rivers”?
拖动视角绕地球转一圈：海面上的洋流箭头，与它上方那一层更细的风箭头顶着同一个方向: Drag to rotate the view around the globe: each current arrow on the sea surface points the same way as the thinner wind arrow layer above it
赤道两侧：信风箭头向西，洋流箭头也向西（北赤道暖流 12°N→14°N，dLon: On both sides of the equator: trade-wind arrows point west, and so do the current arrows (North Equatorial Current 12°N→14°N, dLon = −1); in mid-latitude seas: westerly arrows point east, and so do the current arrows (North Pacific Current 34°N→46°N, dLon = +1)
教材假设：地球表面均匀时，风向由气压带与风带决定: Textbook assumption: on a uniform Earth surface, wind direction is set by pressure belts and wind belts
盛行风吹拂海面，推动海水随风漂流，并使上层海水带动下层海水流动，在海洋表层形成规: Prevailing winds blow over the sea, pushing the water to drift with the wind; the upper water drags the water below, forming large-scale currents in the ocean surface layer.
洋流是「常年比较稳定地沿着一定方向作大规模的流动」，规模远超过河流的流量。: A current is a “large-scale flow in a fairly stable direction year-round,” far larger than the flow of any river.
洋流方向还受海陆分布、地转偏向力等因素影响：所以它并不总与风向完全一致。: Current direction is also affected by the distribution of land and sea and by the Coriolis force, so it doesn't always match the wind exactly.
去掉这一步：只知道有水在流，不知道是谁在推，后面的每条规律都成了死记。: Without this step: you only know water is flowing, not what pushes it, and every later pattern becomes rote memorization.
常考：世界表层洋流的主要动力是盛行风；洋流方向还受海陆分布和地转偏向力影响。: Common exam point: the main driver of the world's surface currents is prevailing wind; current direction is also affected by land–sea distribution and the Coriolis force.
盛行风吹拂海面，推动海水随风漂流，在海洋表层形成规模很大的洋流；洋流方向还受海陆: Prevailing winds blow over the sea and push the water to drift with them, forming large-scale currents in the ocean surface layer; current direction is also affected by land–sea distribution and the Coriolis force.
信风和西风都在推水，为什么中低纬会推成一个圈？: Trade winds and westerlies both push the water. Why do they make a loop at low–mid latitudes?
把「洋流」滑块依次走过 北赤道暖流 → 日本暖流 → 北太平洋暖流 → 加利福尼: Move the “Current” slider through North Equatorial Current → Kuroshio Current → North Pacific Current → California Current and watch how the four arrows join end to end
北赤道暖流自东向西 → 撞上大洋西岸后沿西岸向北成日本暖流 → 到中纬被西风带成: North Equatorial Current flows east to west → hits the ocean's western coast and turns north along it as the Kuroshio Current → at mid-latitudes the westerlies carry it east as the North Pacific Current → at the ocean's eastern coast it turns toward low latitudes, flowing south as the California Current → back at the equator the loop closes: clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere (spinZ −1), with the center symbol turning clockwise; the same winds drive a counterclockwise loop in the Southern Hemisphere (spinZ +1)
信风 + 西风 + 陆地阻挡 → 中低纬环流: Trade winds + westerlies + land barriers → low–mid latitude gyres
北半球顺时针 · 南半球逆时针: Clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere · counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere
信风把赤道两侧的海水自东向西推到大洋西岸，受陆地阻挡后，大部分海水沿西岸流向较高: Trade winds push water on both sides of the equator from east to west toward the ocean's western coast; blocked by land, most of it flows along the west coast toward higher latitudes.
到中纬度海区，在盛行西风吹拂下，洋流转为自西向东流；到大洋东岸又有一部分折向低纬: In mid-latitude seas, driven by the prevailing westerlies, the current turns to flow west to east; at the ocean's eastern coast part of it turns back toward low latitudes.
这样在中低纬海区闭合成大洋环流：北半球呈顺时针方向流动，南半球呈逆时针方向流动。: This closes an ocean gyre at low–mid latitudes: clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
去掉这一步：只会背「北顺南逆」，说不出为什么；换一个半球就把方向画反。: Without this step: you can only recite “clockwise north, counterclockwise south” without knowing why, and you draw it backwards in the other hemisphere.
易错：北半球中低纬环流是顺时针、南半球中低纬是逆时针；北半球中高纬才是逆时针。: Common mistake: low–mid latitude gyres are clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and counterclockwise in the Southern; it is the Northern Hemisphere's mid–high latitudes that are counterclockwise.
信风向西推、西风向东推，加上陆地阻挡，中低纬海区才闭合成大洋环流：北半球顺时针、: Trade winds push west, westerlies push east, and land blocks the flow, so the low–mid latitude seas close into ocean gyres: clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, counterclockwise in the Southern.

极地东风 + 盛行西风 → 中高纬逆时针: Polar easterlies + prevailing westerlies → counterclockwise at mid–high latitudes
北半球中高纬：逆时针，与中低纬反号: Northern mid–high latitudes: counterclockwise, opposite to low–mid latitudes
在北半球中高纬度海区也形成大洋环流，它呈逆时针方向流动。: An ocean gyre also forms in the Northern Hemisphere's mid–high latitude seas, and it flows counterclockwise.
原因在这一带的盛行风：北侧是极地东风（向西南吹），南侧是盛行西风（向东北吹），两: The cause is the prevailing winds here: polar easterlies on the north side (blowing southwest) and prevailing westerlies on the south side (blowing northeast) go opposite ways, so the gyre turns the other way.
千岛寒流（56°N→37°N，ΔT −8.5 ℃）、拉布拉多寒流、东格陵兰寒流都: The Oyashio Current (56°N→37°N, ΔT −8.5 ℃), the Labrador Current and the East Greenland Current all belong to this counterclockwise gyre; the North Atlantic Drift is the edge it shares with the low–mid latitude gyre (belongs to both), so it stays lit when you drag to the Labrador Current. The 3 cold currents at northern mid–high latitudes all have spinZ +1, opposite to the 8 low–mid latitude currents at −1.
去掉这一步：会以为整个北半球的洋流都朝同一个方向转。: Without this step: you'd think all currents in the Northern Hemisphere turn the same way.
常考：北半球中高纬大洋环流呈逆时针方向流动，与中低纬的顺时针相反。: Common exam point: the Northern Hemisphere's mid–high latitude gyres flow counterclockwise, opposite to the clockwise low–mid latitude gyres.
北半球中高纬海区也形成大洋环流，呈逆时针方向流动——因为北侧极地东风向西、南侧盛: An ocean gyre also forms in the Northern Hemisphere's mid–high latitude seas, flowing counterclockwise, because the polar easterlies on the north side blow west and the prevailing westerlies on the south side blow east.

把「洋流」滑块从墨西哥湾暖流拖到加那利寒流，盯住小读数里的 ΔT 和它的正负号: Drag the “Current” slider from the Gulf Stream to the Canary Current and watch ΔT and its sign in the small readout
墨西哥湾暖流：源地 24°N 的表层水温比流经的 40°N 高 6.0 ℃（ΔT: Gulf Stream: surface water at its source, 24°N, is 6.0 ℃ warmer than at 40°N where it flows (ΔT +6.0) → warm current; Canary Current: its source at 42°N is 8.5 ℃ colder than 18°N where it flows (ΔT −8.5) → cold current. The North and South Equatorial Currents, the Equatorial Countercurrent, the Guinea Current, the West Wind Drift and the monsoon currents, 10 in all, are zonal flows; the small readout says “Zonal flow · criterion not applicable,” and warm/cold follows the textbook legend
ΔT = 源地水温 − 流经海区水温: ΔT = source water temperature − water temperature where it flows
ΔT > 0 → 暖流；ΔT < 0 → 寒流（教材按水温判）: ΔT > 0 → warm current; ΔT < 0 → cold current (textbook uses water temperature)
按海水温度，可以把洋流分为暖流和寒流：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域的洋流叫暖流: By seawater temperature, currents are classed as warm or cold: a current flowing from warmer to colder waters is a warm current; the reverse is a cold current.
判据是两地的水温之差，不是「从低纬流向高纬」——那只是一种常见情形。: The criterion is the temperature difference between the two places, not “flowing from low to high latitude,” which is just a common case.
洋流把水体本身搬走，水温随之平流，所以它给经过的海区加热或冷却；这正是暖流增温、: A current carries the water itself, and its temperature moves with it, so it heats or cools the seas it passes; that is why warm currents raise temperatures and cold currents lower them.
去掉这一步：遇到西风漂流、季风洋流这类纬向流，就会按纬度方向把它们判错。: Without this step: when you meet zonal flows like the West Wind Drift or monsoon currents, you'll classify them wrongly by latitude.
易错：用「从低纬流向高纬」判暖流。正确判据是水温：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域: Common mistake: judging a warm current by “flows from low to high latitude.” The correct criterion is water temperature: flowing from warmer to colder waters = warm current.
寒暖按水温判：从水温高的海域流向水温低的海域是暖流，反之是寒流；纬向流本课的温差: Warm or cold is judged by water temperature: flowing from warmer to colder waters is a warm current, the reverse a cold current; this lesson's temperature-difference criterion does not apply to zonal flows, which follow the textbook legend.
南半球的西风漂流为什么不绕圈？北印度洋的洋流为什么会倒过来流？: Why doesn't the Southern Hemisphere's West Wind Drift form a loop? Why do the North Indian Ocean currents reverse?
把「月份」从 1 月拖到 7 月，盯住北印度洋那几条箭头和中心符号的转向: Drag “Month” from January to July and watch the North Indian Ocean arrows and which way the center symbol turns
北印度洋的季风洋流：1 月向西、逆时针（flowEW −1、spinZ +1）；: North Indian Ocean monsoon currents: in January westward and counterclockwise (flowEW −1, spinZ +1); in July eastward and clockwise (flowEW +1, spinZ −1), both signs flip together; April and October show “Transition,” with no direction. On the same screen the Southern Hemisphere's West Wind Drift (50°S–52°S, circling Antarctica, 13 vertices, net longitude +360°, flowEW +1) flows west to east all year and does not reverse with the seasons
季节风向反 → 北印度洋海水反向: Seasonal winds reverse → North Indian Ocean water reverses
冬季向西逆时针 · 夏季向东顺时针: Winter: westward, counterclockwise · Summer: eastward, clockwise
北印度洋海区冬季盛行东北风，海水向西流动、呈逆时针方向旋转；夏季盛行西南风，海水: In the North Indian Ocean, the northeast wind prevails in winter, so the water flows west and turns counterclockwise; the southwest wind prevails in summer, so the water flows east and turns clockwise.
南半球的西风漂流：南极大陆外围海面广阔，终年受西风影响，自西向东流动，教材没有给: The Southern Hemisphere's West Wind Drift: the sea around Antarctica is vast and under westerlies all year, so it flows west to east; the textbook gives it no closed gyre.
两条都不成完整的圈，但原因不同：一条是海区被大陆半包围、盛行风随季节反向；一条是: Neither forms a complete loop, but for different reasons: one sea is half-enclosed by land with prevailing winds that reverse by season; the other is open ocean under westerlies all year.
去掉这一步：会把「南半球中高纬也有闭合大洋环流」和「北印度洋洋流全年朝一个方向」: Without this step: you'll wrongly remember both “the Southern Hemisphere's mid–high latitudes have a closed gyre too” and “North Indian Ocean currents flow one way all year.”
易错：北印度洋季风洋流方向记反——冬季东北风→向西→逆时针，夏季西南风→向东→顺: Common mistake: getting the North Indian Ocean monsoon current backwards. Winter northeast wind → westward → counterclockwise; summer southwest wind → eastward → clockwise.
北印度洋的季风洋流随季风反向（冬季向西逆时针、夏季向东顺时针）；南半球的西风漂流: North Indian Ocean monsoon currents reverse with the monsoon (westward and counterclockwise in winter, eastward and clockwise in summer); the Southern Hemisphere's West Wind Drift flows west to east around Antarctica all year and is not a closed gyre.

Same-latitude comparison (55°N–70°N): the west coast, along Labrador, is affected by the Labrador Current (ΔT −8.8 ℃), and coastal air is 9.6 ℃ colder; drag to the North Atlantic Drift (44°N→62°N, ΔT +8.3 ℃) and the east coast, along Western Europe, is 9.1 ℃ warmer. The difference between the coasts is 18.8 ℃, within the textbook's range of “at 55°N–70°N, the coldest-month mean temperature on the Atlantic's east coast is 16–20 ℃ higher than on the west coast” (the starting Canary Current, ΔT −8.5 ℃, lies farther south off northwest Africa and is not part of this same-latitude comparison). On the equator, the Galápagos Islands (92°W) average about 24.7 ℃ a year with 578 mm of annual rain, cooler and drier than rainforest at the same latitude, because the Peru Current (ΔT −6.7 ℃) makes coastal air 7.4 ℃ colder

由于大洋东部和西部洋流性质不同，同纬度大洋东岸和西岸的气温存在差异。: Because currents on the eastern and western sides of an ocean differ, east and west coasts at the same latitude have different temperatures.

去掉这一步：会把暖流对气候的影响说成「降温」，也会解释不了同纬度东西岸景观为什么: Without this step: you might say warm currents “cool” the climate, and you can't explain why east and west coasts at the same latitude look so different.

寒流和暖流交汇处海水扰动强烈，沉积于海底的营养物质上涌，浮游生物繁盛，鱼类聚集，: Where cold and warm currents meet, the water is strongly stirred, nutrients settled on the seabed rise, plankton thrive, fish gather, and a large fishery forms.
秘鲁沿海在东南信风吹拂下表层海水偏离海岸，深部冷水带着海底的营养物质上涌，也形成: Off Peru, the southeast trade winds push surface water away from the coast, and deep cold water rises carrying nutrients from the seabed, forming another world-famous fishery.

转一周是 1 个太阳日 = 24 时；以遥远的恒星为参照是 23 时 56 分: One turn is 1 solar day = 24 h; measured against distant stars it is 23 h 56 min 4 s (the sidereal day), which is the true rotation period.
角速度除南北两极点外各纬相同，约 15°/时；线速度自赤道向两极递减，两极点的角: Angular speed is the same at all latitudes except the two poles, about 15°/h; linear speed decreases from the equator toward the poles, and at the poles both angular and linear speed are 0.
去掉这一步：不知道为什么晨昏线是从东往西扫过地面，也不知道地方时为什么东早西晚。: Without this step: you can't explain why the terminator sweeps over the ground from east to west, or why local time is earlier in the east.
常考：从北极上空看逆时针、南极上空看顺时针；自转线速度自赤道向两极递减，两极为零: Common exam point: counterclockwise seen from above the North Pole, clockwise from above the South Pole; rotational linear speed decreases from the equator to the poles, where it is zero.
地球绕地轴自西向东自转，周期 1 个太阳日 = 24 时（恒星日 23 时 56: Earth rotates west to east about its axis with a period of 1 solar day = 24 h (the sidereal day, 23 h 56 min 4 s, is the true period); angular speed is about 15°/h, and linear speed decreases from the equator toward the poles.

地球绕太阳走一圈，轨道和速度有什么讲究？: What's special about the orbit and speed as Earth goes around the Sun?
把日期从夏至（172 日）拖到冬至（356 日），看地球走到轨道另一侧、日地距离: Drag the date from the June solstice (day 172) to the December solstice (day 356) and watch Earth move to the other side of its orbit as the Earth–Sun distance shrinks to 147.2 million km
地球沿近似正圆的椭圆轨道自西向东绕太阳公转，太阳在一个焦点上；从夏至（1.520: Earth revolves west to east around the Sun on a nearly circular ellipse, with the Sun at one focus; from the June solstice (152.0 million km, 29.3 km/s) to the December solstice (147.2 million km, 30.3 km/s), the axis stays tilted 23°26′ and keeps the same direction in space
近日点（1 月初）快 · 远日点（7 月初）慢: Perihelion (early Jan) fast · Aphelion (early Jul) slow
地轴与轨道面成 23°26′，空间指向不变: The axis is at 23°26′ to the orbital plane and keeps its direction in space
公转方向也是自西向东，与自转一致；一周是 1 年（回归年 365 日 5 时 4: Revolution is also west to east, the same as rotation; one orbit is 1 year (tropical year 365 d 5 h 48 min 46 s).
轨道是近似正圆的椭圆，太阳位于椭圆的一个焦点上；1 月初经过近日点（1.471: The orbit is a nearly circular ellipse with the Sun at one focus; Earth passes perihelion in early January (147.1 million km) and aphelion in early July (152.1 million km).
日地距离只变 3 % 左右，但公转速度随之变化：近日点线速度 30.3 km/s: The Earth–Sun distance changes by only about 3 %, but orbital speed changes with it: at perihelion, linear speed 30.3 km/s and angular speed 61′/day; at aphelion, 29.3 km/s and 57′/day. The axis keeps its direction in space.
去掉这一步：解释不了北半球夏半年 186 天为什么比冬半年 179 天长——冬半: Without this step: you can't explain why the Northern Hemisphere's summer half-year (186 days) is longer than its winter half-year (179 days): the winter half-year includes perihelion, when Earth moves faster.
常考：1 月初近日点、7 月初远日点；近日点公转速度（线速度和角速度）都大。: Common exam point: perihelion in early January, aphelion in early July; orbital speed (both linear and angular) is greater at perihelion.
公转方向与自转一致（自西向东），轨道是近似正圆的椭圆、太阳在一个焦点上；1 月初: Revolution runs the same way as rotation (west to east) on a nearly circular ellipse with the Sun at one focus; perihelion is in early January and aphelion in early July, and Earth moves faster at perihelion, so the Northern Hemisphere's summer half-year is 7 days longer than its winter half-year.
facts A2.2 第 1、2、4、6、7 条（教材 p.3–4、p.14）、: facts A2.2 items 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 (textbook p.3–4, p.14), item 8 (Fig. 1.4 note, L1)
同一时刻，为什么一半是白天、一半是黑夜？: At any moment, why is half the world in daylight and half in darkness?
把世界时从 0 拖到 12，看地球在晨昏线下面转: Drag UTC from 0 to 12 and watch Earth turn beneath the terminator
太阳只能照亮地球的一半：向着太阳的是昼半球、背着的是夜半球，分界线就是晨昏线圈；: The Sun can only light half of Earth: the half facing it is the day hemisphere, the half facing away is the night hemisphere, and the boundary is the terminator circle; on the June solstice the terminator just touches the Arctic Circle, so everything inside it is in the day hemisphere
同一时刻，太阳只能照亮地球表面的一半：向着太阳的半球是白昼（昼半球），背着太阳的: At any moment, the Sun can only light half of Earth's surface: the half facing the Sun has daytime (day hemisphere), and the half facing away has night (night hemisphere).
昼半球和夜半球的分界线（圈），叫作晨昏线（圈）。这一圈所在的平面永远正对太阳，所: The boundary line (circle) between the day and night hemispheres is called the terminator (circle). Its plane always faces the Sun, so it doesn't turn with Earth; Earth turns beneath it.
昼夜交替的周期是 1 个太阳日；这样的周期长短适宜，白昼不会过于炎热、黑夜不会过: Day and night alternate with a period of 1 solar day; this period is just right, so days don't get too hot and nights don't get too cold.
去掉这一步：只会说「天亮了天黑了」，说不出那条线是什么、为什么会动。: Without this step: you can only say “it got light, it got dark”, without saying what that line is or why it moves.
易错：昼夜交替是地球自转造成的，周期 1 个太阳日（不是公转、不是 1 年）。: Common mistake: day and night alternate because Earth rotates, with a period of 1 solar day (not revolution, not 1 year).
太阳只能照亮地球表面的一半，昼半球和夜半球的分界线（圈）叫晨昏线（圈）；地球自转: The Sun can only light half of Earth's surface, and the boundary line (circle) between the day and night hemispheres is the terminator (circle); Earth's rotation makes day and night keep alternating, with a period of 1 solar day.
晨昏线上，哪一半是晨线、哪一半是昏线？: On the terminator, which half is the dawn line and which is the dusk line?
点一下地球上那半圈琥珀色的线（顺着自转方向由夜进昼的那半圈）: Click the amber half-circle on Earth (the half going from night into day in the direction of rotation)
顺自转方向（自西向东）由夜半球进入昼半球的那半圈是晨线（琥珀色），由昼半球进入夜: In the direction of rotation (west to east), the half going from the night hemisphere into the day hemisphere is the dawn line (amber), and the half going from day into night is the dusk line (indigo); the Sun's altitude is 0° at every point on both
顺自转方向：由夜进昼 = 晨线；由昼进夜 = 昏线: In the direction of rotation: night into day = dawn line; day into night = dusk line
晨昏线上太阳高度 0°；直射点上是 90°: Sun's altitude is 0° on the terminator; 90° at the subsolar point
一条晨昏圈上，一半是晨线、一半是昏线，判据是自转方向：顺着自转方向由夜进昼的就是: Half of the terminator circle is the dawn line and half the dusk line, judged by the direction of rotation: the half going from night into day in the direction of rotation is the dawn line.
由昼进夜的另外一半是昏线；地球转下去，晨线上的地方迎来日出，昏线上的地方迎来日落: The other half, going from day into night, is the dusk line; as Earth turns, places on the dawn line see sunrise and places on the dusk line see sunset.
晨昏线上各点的太阳高度都是 0°（太阳刚在地平线上）；太阳直射点上太阳高度是 9: The Sun's altitude is 0° at every point on the terminator (the Sun is right on the horizon); at the subsolar point it is 90°.
去掉这一步：看到一条线却分不出晨昏，判断不了某地是日出还是日落。: Without this step: you see a line but can't tell dawn from dusk, so you can't decide whether a place is at sunrise or sunset.
易错：判晨昏要沿自转方向（自西向东）看，不是沿经线往北看；晨线以东是昼半球。: Common mistake: judge dawn or dusk along the direction of rotation (west to east), not northward along a meridian; east of the dawn line is the day hemisphere.
顺自转方向由夜半球进入昼半球的那半圈是晨线，由昼半球进入夜半球的那半圈是昏线；晨: In the direction of rotation, the half going from the night hemisphere into the day hemisphere is the dawn line, and the half going from day into night is the dusk line; the Sun's altitude on the terminator is 0°.
facts A2.3 第 1 条（p.7）、A2.6 第 1 条（p.11）、B: facts A2.3 item 1 (p.7), A2.6 item 1 (p.11), B2.9 rule
东边的城市为什么先看到日出？: Why do cities farther east see sunrise first?
把经度从 180°W 拖到 180°E，盯住中控台的地方时读数: Drag longitude from 180°W to 180°E and watch the local time reading on the console
地方时 04:00 → 08:00（0° 经线）→ 16:00（180°E）：每: Local time 04:00 → 08:00 (0° meridian) → 16:00 (180°E): every 15° east, local time is 1 hour ahead; at the same instant, different longitudes have different local times
东边比西边早 · 经度每隔 15°，地方时差 1 小时: East is ahead of west · every 15° of longitude, local time differs by 1 hour
地球自西向东转，同一纬度上东边的地点比西边的地点先看到日出，时间也就有了早迟之分: Earth turns west to east, so at the same latitude places to the east see sunrise before places to the west, and their clocks are ahead.
经度每隔 15°，地方时相差 1 小时（1° = 4 分钟）；越在东边，时间越早: Every 15° of longitude, local time differs by 1 hour (1° = 4 minutes); the farther east, the further ahead the clock.
地方时只跟经度有关、跟纬度无关：同一条经线上各地的地方时相同。: Local time depends only on longitude, not latitude: all places on the same meridian have the same local time.
去掉这一步：算不出两地的时间差，后面的时区、区时、日界线全接不上。: Without this step: you can't work out the time difference between two places, and time zones, zone time and the date line all fall apart.
常考：给两地经度算地方时差；「北京时间」是东八区的区时（东经 120° 的地方时: Common exam point: given two longitudes, find the local time difference; “Beijing Time” is the zone time of UTC+8 (local time at 120°E), not the local time of Beijing (116°E).
地球自西向东转，东边的地点比西边的先看到日出、时间更早；经度每隔 15° 地方时: Earth turns west to east, so places to the east see sunrise before places to the west and are ahead in time; every 15° of longitude, local time differs by 1 hour.
全世界都用地方时不行，怎么办？跨过 180° 为什么回到昨天？: The whole world can't run on local time, so what then? Why does crossing 180° take you back to yesterday?
把经度从 180°E 拖过 180° 到 180°W，盯住中控台说明行里的区时和: Drag longitude from 180°E across 180° to 180°W and watch the zone time and date in the console info line
东经 180°（东十二区）与西经 180°（西十二区）钟表时间都是 16:00，: At 180°E (UTC+12) and 180°W (UTC−12) the clocks both read 16:00, but the dates differ by one day: June 21 in UTC+12, June 20 in UTC−12
全球 24 个时区 · 每区 15° · 相邻区时差 1 小时: 24 time zones worldwide · 15° each · neighboring zones differ by 1 hour
北京时间 = 东八区区时 = 东经 120° 的地方时: Beijing Time = UTC+8 zone time = local time at 120°E
地方时太碎没法用：全球分 24 个时区、每区跨 15°，以中央经线的地方时为区时: Local times are too fragmented to use, so the world is divided into 24 time zones, each spanning 15°, using the local time of its central meridian as zone time; neighboring zones differ by 1 hour, with the east ahead.
东十二区和西十二区各跨 7.5°、合为一个时区：区时相同，但日期差一天（东十二区: UTC+12 and UTC−12 each span 7.5° and together form one time zone: same clock time, but the dates differ by one day (UTC+12 is a day ahead of UTC−12).
原则上以 180° 经线为「今天」和「昨天」的分界线：自东十二区向东进入西十二区: In principle the 180° meridian separates “today” from “yesterday”: going east from UTC+12 into UTC−12, the time stays the same and the date goes back one day; going the other way, the date goes forward one day.
去掉这一步：跨日界线的日期会算错——教材里 F-22 战斗机导航系统失灵，就是电: Without this step: dates across the date line come out wrong. In the textbook, F-22 fighter jets lost their navigation systems because the electronics ignored the date change at the date line.
易错：自西向东越过 180° 经线，日期减一天（很多同学记反）；东十二区比西十二: Common mistake: crossing the 180° meridian from west to east, the date goes back one day (many students get this backwards); UTC+12 is a day ahead of UTC−12.
全球分 24 个时区、每区跨 15°，区时取中央经线的地方时；以 180° 经线: The world is divided into 24 time zones, each spanning 15°, with zone time taken from the local time of the central meridian; the 180° meridian is used for the International Date Line, and going east from UTC+12 into UTC−12 the time stays the same and the date goes back one day.
facts A2.4 第 2–4、7–8 条（教材 p.8–10）、B2.6、B: facts A2.4 items 2–4, 7–8 (textbook p.8–10), B2.6, B2.7
夏至这天，越往北白天越长，长到哪里为止？: On the June solstice, the farther north you go, the longer the day. Where does it stop?
把纬度从 40°N 拖到北极圈（66°34′N），盯住昼长读数: Drag latitude from 40°N to the Arctic Circle (66°34′N) and watch the day length reading
昼长 14.84 h（40°N）→ 24.00 h（北极圈，极昼）；昼弧越来越长: Day length 14.84 h (40°N) → 24.00 h (Arctic Circle, polar day); the day arc keeps growing and the night arc shrinking; at the equator it is 12.00 h on every day of the year
夏至：40°N 14.84 h，极圈以北极昼: June solstice: 40°N 14.84 h, polar day north of the Arctic Circle
晨昏线把所经过的纬线分成昼弧和夜弧：昼弧比夜弧长就昼长夜短，反之则昼短夜长。: The terminator divides each parallel it crosses into a day arc and a night arc: if the day arc is longer, days are longer than nights, and vice versa.
夏至太阳直射北回归线：北半球昼最长、夜最短，纬度越高昼越长，北极圈及其以北都是极: On the June solstice the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer: the Northern Hemisphere has its longest day and shortest night, the higher the latitude the longer the day, and the Arctic Circle and everything north of it have polar day; the Southern Hemisphere is the opposite.
冬至反过来：北半球昼最短、夜最长，北极圈以北极夜。把日期拖到春分对比一下：晨昏线: The December solstice is the reverse: the Northern Hemisphere has its shortest day and longest night, with polar night north of the Arctic Circle. Drag the date to the March equinox to compare: the terminator passes through both poles and every place has 12 hours.
去掉这一步：解释不了为什么哈尔滨的夏天比广州白天长、而冬天反过来。: Without this step: you can't explain why Harbin has longer summer days than Guangzhou, but shorter winter days.
易错：赤道上也有昼夜交替，但全年没有昼夜长短变化；极昼就是昼长 24 小时。: Common mistake: the equator does have day and night, but its day length never changes during the year; polar day means a 24-hour day.
昼长随纬度与季节变化：夏至北半球昼长夜短、纬度越高昼越长，北极圈以北极昼；赤道与: Day length varies with latitude and season: on the June solstice, Northern Hemisphere days are longer than nights, and the higher the latitude the longer the day, with polar day north of the Arctic Circle; at the equator, and everywhere on the equinoxes, day and night are both 12 h.
facts A2.5 第 1–4 条（教材 p.11）、B2.4、B2.12、图: facts A2.5 items 1–4 (textbook p.11), B2.4, B2.12, Fig. 1.16
正午的太阳有多高，能不能到头顶？: How high is the noon Sun? Can it be directly overhead?
把日期从夏至（172 日）拖到冬至（356 日），盯住正午太阳高度读数: Drag the date from the June solstice (day 172) to the December solstice (day 356) and watch the noon sun angle reading
北京（40°N）正午太阳高度 73.4°（夏至 73°26′）→ 26.6°（冬: Noon sun angle in Beijing (40°N) 73.4° (June solstice 73°26′) → 26.6° (December solstice 26°34′); the subsolar point moves from the Tropic of Cancer to the Tropic of Capricorn
太阳高度是太阳光线与地平面的交角：直射点上 90°、晨昏线上 0°；正午太阳高度: The Sun's altitude is the angle between sunlight and the ground plane: 90° at the subsolar point, 0° on the terminator; the noon sun angle is the highest the Sun gets that day.
H = 90° − |φ − δ|，离直射点纬度越近越大；40°N 夏至 73°: H = 90° − |φ − δ|: the closer to the subsolar latitude, the larger; at 40°N, 73°26′ on the June solstice and 26°34′ on the December solstice.
纬度分布：二分日由赤道向南北降低、夏至由北回归线、冬至由南回归线降低；北回归线以: By latitude: on the equinoxes it falls from the equator toward both poles; on the June solstice from the Tropic of Cancer; on the December solstice from the Tropic of Capricorn. North of the Tropic of Cancer, the noon Sun is always to the south.
去掉这一步：说不出为什么同在夏天广州比北京晒得更狠，也解释不了楼间距为什么按冬至: Without this step: you can't explain why Guangzhou's summer sun is fiercer than Beijing's, or why building spacing is calculated for the December solstice.
常考：用 H = 90° − |φ − δ| 算正午太阳高度；北回归线以北正午太: Common exam point: find the noon sun angle with H = 90° − |φ − δ|; north of the Tropic of Cancer the noon Sun is in the south all year, so shadows point north.
正午太阳高度 H = 90° − |φ − δ|，离直射点越近越大；40°N 夏: Noon sun angle H = 90° − |φ − δ|: the closer to the subsolar point, the larger; at 40°N, 73°26′ on the June solstice and 26°34′ on the December solstice; north of the Tropic of Cancer the noon Sun is in the south all year.
考核：世界杯在莫斯科开幕，北京时间是几点？: Test: the World Cup opens in Moscow. What time is it in Beijing?
把经度调到 120°E、世界时调到 14.5 时、日期调到 6 月 14 日，让: Set longitude to 120°E, UTC to 14.5 h and the date to June 14, so Beijing's local time reads 22:30
达标：北京地方时 22:30、东八区、日期 6 月 14 日；中途世界时会被拨到: Target met: Beijing local time 22:30, UTC+8, date June 14; partway through, UTC will be moved to 08:00 and you'll need to set it back
先看两地相差几个时区：莫斯科东三区、北京东八区，差 5 个时区。: First find how many time zones apart they are: Moscow is UTC+3, Beijing UTC+8, so 5 zones apart.
越在东边时间越早，所以北京时间 = 17:30 + 5 时 = 22:30。: The farther east, the further ahead the clock, so Beijing Time = 17:30 + 5 h = 22:30.
北京时间是东八区的区时，也就是东经 120° 的地方时，不是北京（116°E）的: Beijing Time is the zone time of UTC+8, which is the local time at 120°E, not the local time of Beijing (116°E).
去掉这一步：出门旅行、看国际赛事时间、算跨日界线的航班日期都会错。: Without this step: you'll get it wrong when traveling, checking international match times, or working out flight dates across the date line.
常考：给两地时区算区时；跨日界线时「时间不变、日期变」。: Common exam point: given two time zones, find zone time; crossing the date line, “the time stays the same, the date changes”.
莫斯科东三区当地 17:30 开幕，北京在东八区，相差 5 个时区，所以北京时间: The opening is at 17:30 local time in Moscow (UTC+3); Beijing is UTC+8, 5 zones apart, so it's 22:30 Beijing Time.
地轴 · 指向北极星附近，空间指向不变: Earth's axis · points near Polaris, fixed direction in space
昏线：由昼进夜（在背面）: Dusk line: day into night (on the far side)
地球自转一周的时间，作为自转真正周期的那个是: Which of these is Earth's true rotation period?
教材 p.2：以太阳为参照是太阳日 24 时，以遥远的恒星为参照是 23 时 5: Textbook p.2: measured against the Sun it is the solar day of 24 h; measured against distant stars it is 23 h 56 min 4 s, and the sidereal day is Earth's true rotation period.
地球自转的角速度和线速度，正确的是: Which statement about Earth's rotational angular and linear speed is correct?
各纬度角速度相同，线速度也相同: Angular speed and linear speed are both the same at all latitudes
角速度除两极点外各纬相同，线速度自赤道向两极递减: Angular speed is the same at all latitudes except the poles; linear speed decreases from the equator toward the poles
角速度赤道最大，线速度各纬相同: Angular speed is greatest at the equator; linear speed is the same at all latitudes
两极点的角速度最大: Angular speed is greatest at the poles
教材 p.3 与 p.14 要点 1：角速度除南北两极点外各纬相等（约 15°/: Textbook p.3 and p.14 key point 1: angular speed is equal at all latitudes except the North and South Poles (about 15°/h); linear speed decreases from the equator toward the poles.
关于近日点和远日点，正确的是: Which statement about perihelion and aphelion is correct?
7 月初近日点，公转速度快: Perihelion in early July, orbital speed fast
1 月初近日点，公转速度快: Perihelion in early January, orbital speed fast

三档开关的最后一档（纸带歪斜）把摩擦放大到 2.5 倍，δ 从 −1.28 %: The last position of the three-way switch (tape slanted) multiplies friction by 2.5, and δ drops from −1.28 % to −3.21 %.
实验素养：说出误差来源与方向（课标 p.16「知道实验存在误差」；A7.4）。: Lab literacy: state the source and direction of error (curriculum standard p.16: “know that experiments have errors”; A7.4).
给你一条打好的纸带，不查表、不算加速度，能不能把当地的 g 测出来？: Given a finished tape, with no tables and no acceleration calculation, can you measure the local g?
记满 3 组以上、测点不同、同一个重物，让 ½v²–h 的过原点斜率与 9.8: Record 3 or more sets at different points with the same weight, so the ½v²–h slope through the origin is within 2 % of 9.8 m/s²
达标条件：① 记满 3 组以上；② 每组取不同的测点；③ 三次记录同一个重物；④: Target conditions: ① 3 or more sets recorded; ② a different point for each set; ③ the same weight for all records; ④ slope through the origin within 2 % of 9.8 m/s². One valid answer: 0.200 kg, ideal setting, record dots 4/7/10/13 → k = 9.80, 0.00 % off (Real · vertical · 0.200 kg also passes: k = 9.68, −1.18 %). Counterexamples: 0.050 kg on the real setting k = 9.31, −5.00 %; tape slanted k = 9.49, −3.17 %.
没有新结论：把前七步连起来用一遍——选点、量 h、算 v、作图，斜率就是 g。这: Nothing new: run through the first seven steps together. Choose dots, measure h, find v, plot, and the slope is g. This is the quantitative test of the law of conservation of mechanical energy on textbook p.92.
facts A2.7、A2.14、A7.4、A7.5；p.92、p.96；B3: facts A2.7, A2.14, A7.4, A7.5; p.92, p.96; B3 item 4, Standard values tables E, F
先按 k ≈ 9.8 估一下斜率，再看记的组数够不够（≥ 3 组、测点不同）。: First estimate the slope as k ≈ 9.8, then check you have enough sets (≥ 3, at different points).
三组必须是同一个重物，中途换质量会把斜率搞乱（判据会判不通过）。: All sets must use the same weight; changing mass midway messes up the slope (and the check will fail).
真实档也能过，但要选较重的重物 + 纸带竖直。: The real setting can pass too, but choose a heavier weight + vertical tape.
没有新结论：把前七步连起来用一遍就是考核。: Nothing new: running through the first seven steps together is the test.
综合：选点 + 量 h + 算 v + 过原点斜率 = g。: Synthesis: choose dots + measure h + find v + slope through origin = g.

记录一组开始画: Record a set to start plotting

先释放重物，再接通电源: Release the weight first, then switch on the power
先接通电源，再释放重物: Switch on the power first, then release the weight
先断电再释放重物: Switch off the power first, then release the weight

以 h 为横轴、½v² 为纵轴作图，若机械能守恒，图线应当是: Plotting with h on the horizontal axis and ½v² on the vertical axis, if mechanical energy is conserved, the graph should be
一条过原点的直线，斜率 ≈ g: A straight line through the origin, slope ≈ g
一条不过原点的直线: A straight line not through the origin
½v² = gh（m 消去）：过原点、斜率就是 g；差值（斜率偏小）来自阻力。: ½v² = gh (m cancels): through the origin, and the slope is g; any gap (smaller slope) comes from resistance.
真实实验里，重力势能的减少量略大于动能的增加量，主要原因是: In a real experiment, the decrease in gravitational PE is slightly larger than the increase in KE, mainly because
重物的质量测错了: The mass of the weight was measured wrongly

用一条打点纸带量出重物下落时的速度与高度，验证 ½v² = gh，并说出阻力让结: Use a dotted paper tape to measure the speed and height of a falling weight, verify ½v² = gh, and say which way resistance pushes the result.

人教版选择性必修 1「自然地理基础」· 第四章第三节「海—气相互作用」（p.72: PEP Elective Vol. 1 “Fundamentals of Physical Geography” · Ch. 4, Sec. 3 “Ocean–Atmosphere Interaction” (pp. 72–76)
海—气相互作用与厄尔尼诺、拉尼娜: Ocean–Atmosphere Interaction: El Niño and La Niña
海温异常 → 温差 → 环流 → 降水: SST anomaly → temperature gap → circulation → rainfall
秘鲁沿海常年干旱，为什么 2016 年底海水一暖，就下起了暴雨、还死了近百人？: The Peruvian coast is dry year-round — so why, when the sea warmed in late 2016, did torrential rain fall and kill nearly a hundred people?
海洋给大气水汽与热量（潜热是主要途径），大气用风驱动表层海水: The ocean gives the atmosphere water vapor and heat (mainly as latent heat); the atmosphere drives the surface water with wind
正常年份：西岸暖、东岸冷（冷水上涌），东西温差 +8.0 ℃: Normal years: warm in the west, cold in the east (upwelling); east–west gap +8.0 ℃
温差驱动大气热力环流：西侧上升、东侧下沉，信风自东向西: The temperature gap drives a thermal circulation: air rises in the west and sinks in the east, with trade winds blowing east to west
东侧海温异常升高 → 温差减小、信风减弱 → 东侧下沉减弱甚至转为上升: SST in the east rises abnormally → gap shrinks, trade winds weaken → sinking in the east weakens or even turns to rising
东岸（秘鲁、智利）由旱转涝，西岸（印尼）转旱；拉尼娜相反: The east coast (Peru, Chile) goes from drought to floods, the west coast (Indonesia) turns dry; La Niña is the reverse
印度尼西亚、澳大利亚一侧的暖海面与上空雨云: Warm sea surface and rain clouds over Indonesia and Australia
南美沿岸的冷海面与冷水上涌: Cold sea surface and upwelling along South America
两岸之间的闭合环流与近地面信风: The closed circulation between the two coasts, with trade winds near the surface
海洋和大气之间到底在换什么？: What exactly do the ocean and atmosphere exchange?
拖动视角看一圈：西边海面暖、东边沿岸冷，两岸的陆地和一条斜贯的赤道线: Drag to rotate the view: warm sea in the west, cold water along the east coast, land on both sides, and the equator running across at an angle
参考工况（正常年份）：东岸海温 21.5 ℃、东西温差 +8.0 ℃、近地面信风: Reference conditions (normal year): east-coast SST 21.5 ℃, east–west gap +8.0 ℃, surface trade winds 6.00 m/s (east to west); the ocean supplies 87.5% of atmospheric water vapor, and the ocean surface layer stores 85% of solar heat
海洋通过蒸发向大气提供水汽——大气中约 87.5 % 的水汽由海洋提供。: The ocean supplies the atmosphere with water vapor through evaporation — about 87.5% of atmospheric water vapor comes from the ocean.
海洋吸收了到达地表太阳辐射的大部分，并把其中 85 % 的热量储存在海洋表层，再: The ocean absorbs most of the solar radiation reaching Earth's surface, stores 85% of that heat in its surface layer, and passes it to the atmosphere as latent heat and longwave radiation.
海水的蒸发—凝结是海—气热量输送的主要途径；反过来，大气主要通过风向海洋传递动能: Evaporation and condensation of seawater are the main route of ocean-to-atmosphere heat transfer; in return, the atmosphere passes kinetic energy to the ocean mainly through wind.
去掉这一步：厄尔尼诺就成了一串没有源头的名词，学生不知道「海水一暖」为什么会牵动: Without this step: El Niño becomes a string of terms with no source, and students don't know why “the sea warming” affects the atmosphere.
常考：海洋是大气最主要的水汽来源和热量储存库；大气为海水运动提供动能。: Frequently tested: the ocean is the atmosphere's main source of water vapor and main heat store; the atmosphere supplies kinetic energy for seawater movement.
海洋向大气提供水汽与热量（潜热是主要途径），大气通过风向海洋传递动能，驱使其表层: The ocean supplies the atmosphere with water vapor and heat (mainly as latent heat), and the atmosphere passes kinetic energy to the ocean through wind, driving its surface water; ocean–atmosphere interaction maintains Earth's balance of water and heat.
为什么东岸比西岸冷那么多？: Why is the east coast so much colder than the west?
把「东岸冷舌涌升强度」从 1.00 拖到 1.20：看东端那支向上弯的箭头变长、: Drag “East-coast upwelling strength” from 1.00 to 1.20: watch the upward-curving arrow at the east end grow longer and the east coast get colder
东岸海温 21.5 → 19.9 ℃；东西温差 +8.0 → +9.6 ℃；信风: East-coast SST 21.5 → 19.9 ℃; east–west gap +8.0 → +9.6 ℃; trade winds 6.00 → 7.20 m/s (stronger)
东岸比西岸冷，是因为信风把表层暖水吹走、下层冷水上涌。: The east coast is colder than the west because the trade winds blow away warm surface water and cold deep water wells up.
上涌越强，东岸越冷：系数 1.00 → 1.20 时东岸 21.5 → 19.9: The stronger the upwelling, the colder the east coast: at a factor of 1.00 → 1.20, the east coast goes 21.5 → 19.9 ℃.
东西温差随之变大（+8.0 → +9.6 ℃），信风也更强（6.00 → 7.2: The east–west gap grows with it (+8.0 → +9.6 ℃), and the trade winds get stronger too (6.00 → 7.20 m/s).
去掉这一步：「东岸为什么冷」只能背结论，后面「厄尔尼诺＝东岸变暖」就没有对照。: Without this step: “why the east coast is cold” can only be memorized, and “El Niño = the east coast warming” has nothing to compare against.
常考：东太平洋沿岸的冷舌由冷水上涌形成，上涌与信风强弱相关。: Frequently tested: the cold tongue along the eastern Pacific coast is formed by upwelling, which depends on the strength of the trade winds.
东岸的冷来自冷水上涌：信风把表层暖水吹走、下层冷水上升；上涌越强，东岸越冷、东西: The cold in the east comes from upwelling: trade winds blow away warm surface water and cold deep water rises; the stronger the upwelling, the colder the east coast and the bigger the east–west gap.
两岸的温差，怎么变成天上的环流？: How does the temperature gap between the coasts become a circulation in the sky?
把这个环流圈补完整：先点西侧那一列气柱（应出现向上箭头），再点东侧那一列（应出现: Complete this circulation cell: first click the air column on the west side (an upward arrow should appear), then the one on the east side (a downward arrow should appear)
西侧上升（+1.000）、东侧下沉（−1.000）、近地面信风 6.00 m/s: Rising in the west (+1.000), sinking in the east (−1.000), surface trade winds 6.00 m/s east to west; once both are clicked correctly, the west-to-east flow aloft and the east-to-west flow near the surface fill in automatically and the loop closes
温差 → 环流：西升 · 东沉: Gap → circulation: rising west · sinking east
近地面信风自东向西: Surface trade winds east to west
正常年份西侧海水温度较高、气流上升；中东部较低、大气较稳定、气流下沉。: In normal years the western sea is warmer and air rises; the central and eastern sea is cooler, the atmosphere is more stable, and air sinks.
近地面信风自东向西，把暖水堆到西侧；高空则相反。: Near the surface the trade winds blow east to west, piling warm water up in the west; aloft the flow is the reverse.
四支箭头连成一个闭合环流圈——这就是教材图 4.18 留给学生画的那个环。: The four arrows join into one closed circulation cell — the loop that textbook Fig. 4.18 leaves for students to draw.
去掉这一步：温差与环流之间没有桥，学生只记住「东岸雨多」这类结果。: Without this step: there's no bridge between the temperature gap and the circulation, and students only remember results like “more rain on the east coast”.
常考：正常年份西侧上升、东侧下沉，近地面信风自东向西（教材图 4.18、活动第: Frequently tested: in normal years air rises in the west and sinks in the east, with surface trade winds blowing east to west (textbook Fig. 4.18, Activity Q1).
正常年份西侧海水暖、气流上升，东侧海温低、气流下沉；近地面信风自东向西，与高空相: In normal years the western sea is warm and air rises, while the eastern sea is cool and air sinks; surface trade winds blow east to west, opposite to the flow aloft, forming a closed thermal circulation.
facts A2.3 #2、图 4.18 图面；B2.2 ④⑤⑥、B4 D2/D: facts A2.3 #2, Fig. 4.18 drawing; B2.2 ④⑤⑥, B4 D2/D3, Activity Q1
东岸海水一暖，环流会怎样？: When the east-coast sea warms, what happens to the circulation?
把「赤道中东部海温异常」拖到 +2.4 ℃（1997—98 强厄尔尼诺）：看东侧: Drag “Central–eastern SST anomaly” to +2.4 ℃ (the strong 1997–98 El Niño): watch the east-side color band warm up and the air column flip from sinking to rising
东岸海温 21.5 → 23.9 ℃；东西温差 +8.0 → +5.6 ℃；信风: East-coast SST 21.5 → 23.9 ℃; east–west gap +8.0 → +5.6 ℃; trade winds 6.00 → 4.20 m/s; east side sinking → rising (+0.600), west-side rising gone (0.000); east-coast rainfall +72.0 mm/month, west coast −45.0 mm/month; status “El Niño · Very strong”
有些年份中东部的表层海水异常升高，就是厄尔尼诺现象。: In some years the surface water in the central and eastern Pacific becomes abnormally warm — this is El Niño.
之后东西温差减小（+8.0 → +5.6 ℃），信风减弱（6.00 → 4.20: As a result the east–west gap shrinks (+8.0 → +5.6 ℃) and the trade winds weaken (6.00 → 4.20 m/s).
东侧下沉减弱、甚至转为上升，东岸由旱转涝（+72 mm/月）；西侧上升减弱，转旱: Sinking in the east weakens or even turns to rising, and the east coast goes from drought to floods (+72 mm/month); rising in the west weakens, and it turns dry (−45 mm/month).
去掉这一步：教材导入的秘鲁洪水（p.72）没有解释。: Without this step: the Peru floods that open the textbook section (p. 72) go unexplained.
易错：把厄尔尼诺说成「东岸变冷」或「信风反向」——是东岸异常变暖、温差减小、信风: Common mistake: describing El Niño as “the east coast cooling” or “the trade winds reversing” — it's the east coast warming abnormally, the gap shrinking and the trade winds weakening.
厄尔尼诺是赤道附近太平洋中东部表层海水异常升高；它使东西温差减小、信风减弱，东侧: El Niño is the abnormal warming of surface water in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific; it shrinks the east–west gap and weakens the trade winds; sinking in the east weakens or even turns to rising; the east coast goes from drought to floods, and the west coast from floods to drought.
到底暖到哪一步，东岸才从「下沉」翻成「上升」？: Exactly how warm does it have to get before the east coast flips from “sinking” to “rising”?
把海温异常拖到 +1.5 ℃：这一点东侧的下沉刚好消失（两边都不升不沉）: Drag the SST anomaly to +1.5 ℃: at this point the sinking in the east just disappears (neither side rises nor sinks)
东侧下沉消失（0.000）、西侧上升消失（0.000）；两岸降水距平同为 ±45: East-side sinking gone (0.000), west-side rising gone (0.000); rainfall anomalies on both coasts are ±45.0 mm/month; east–west gap +6.5 ℃, trade winds 4.88 m/s; status “El Niño · Strong”
教材的原话是「下沉气流减弱或消失，甚至出现上升气流」——中间有一个「消失」的点。: The textbook says “the sinking air weakens or disappears, and rising air may even appear” — there's a point in the middle where it “disappears”.
本课把这一点定在 A = +1.5 ℃（课件设定，与「强」档起点对齐）。: This lesson places that point at A = +1.5 ℃ (lesson setting, aligned with the start of the “Strong” level).
到这一点，两岸的垂直运动都归零、降水距平都是 ±45 mm/月；再暖一点东侧才转: At this point vertical motion on both coasts drops to zero and both rainfall anomalies are ±45 mm/month; only a bit warmer and the east side turns to rising.
去掉这一步：学生会以为「一暖就翻」，说不清「减弱」与「反转」的区别。: Without this step: students think “a little warming flips it” and can't tell “weakening” from “reversing”.
易错：把「减弱 / 消失 / 反向」当成一句话——教材写的是三个阶段。: Common mistake: treating “weakens / disappears / reverses” as one statement — the textbook describes three stages.
东侧下沉「消失」的那一点是海温异常 +1.5 ℃（课件设定）：两岸垂直运动同时归: The point where sinking in the east “disappears” is an SST anomaly of +1.5 ℃ (lesson setting): vertical motion on both coasts drops to zero together, and only a bit warmer does the east side turn to rising.
反过来，东岸更冷会怎样？: The other way round — what happens when the east coast gets colder?
把海温异常拖到 −2.0 ℃（1973—74 拉尼娜）：东西两侧的色带与箭头全部: Drag the SST anomaly to −2.0 ℃ (the 1973–74 La Niña): all the color bands and arrows on both sides reverse
东岸海温 19.5 ℃；东西温差 +10.0 ℃（比正常更大）；信风 7.50: East-coast SST 19.5 ℃; east–west gap +10.0 ℃ (larger than normal); trade winds 7.50 m/s; stronger sinking in the east (−2.333), stronger rising in the west (+2.333); east-coast rainfall −60.0 mm/month, west coast +60.0 mm/month; status “La Niña · Very strong”
温差增大 · 信风更强（教材无拉尼娜图 · 本课示意）: Gap grows · trade winds stronger (no La Niña figure in the textbook · illustrative)
拉尼娜是中东部表层海水温度异常降低，与厄尔尼诺相反。: La Niña is an abnormal cooling of surface water in the central and eastern Pacific, the opposite of El Niño.
